capabilities.scope: On one operator-reported V1.2 sample, normal POWER boot of the R3 NOR FIT and LittleFS image reached NetBSD 11.1 ESP_MOSAICO_LITTLEFS_NOR #6, mounted the 10 MiB littlefs root from flash1 at 0x600000, and reached the final Startup complete message. A subsequent pinned-host-key SSH session succeeded and stayed connected for 52 seconds; WPA status was COMPLETED with SAE and IPv4 present during the session. The /var/run/rc.log interval was 4 minutes 43 seconds with rc exit status 0; the device clock reported a date in 2010, so only the within-log interval is recorded. Earlier bounded tests on this sample reached a single-user shell, retained a synced marker across one normal power cycle, and passed a read-write remount plus write/sync/read smoke check; a RAM-loaded run passed the full VFS checker against the NOR root. This does not establish repeated-cycle reliability, sudden-power-loss durability, full services, NAND, full PSRAM read/write or general peripheral support.

On one operator-reported V1.2 sample, a littlefs root on NOR flash1 (10 MiB at 0x600000) was mounted and operated after a RAM-loaded boot. The read-write remount, full VFS checker and sync passed. A separate ordinary NOR boot reached a single-user shell, retained an earlier synced marker across one normal POWER off/on, and passed a read-write remount plus bounded write/sync/read smoke check. This does not establish crash or sudden-power-loss durability, repeated-cycle reliability, NAND filesystems or sustained operation.

On one operator-reported V1.2 sample, ordinary NOR boot with ESP_MOSAICO_LITTLEFS_NOR kernel #31 and a 10 MiB LittleFS root was followed by one bounded strict-SAE probe. The connected scan preserved the association; ROAM reached the requested alternate BSSID, which matched the final BSSID and differed from baseline. Post-roam status was WPA_COMPLETED/SAE/PMF=1; IPv4 was confirmed with ifconfig, and DNS plus gateway ping passed. A separate later pinned-host-key SSH session after R3 startup remained connected for 52 seconds with WPA COMPLETED/SAE and IPv4 present. These are bounded scenarios, not sustained network acceptance. Host getaddrinfo resolved the assigned .local name to the target interface IPv4. A separate temporary WPA2-PSK profile reached WPA2-PSK/COMPLETED and host ping passed. A later router-side association view showed WPA3-PSK/PMF restored on the original AP. The shared station Action path is now integrated. A RAM probe with EmberBSD 44b8639 preserved SAE/PMF and SSH and reported correlated BTM TX completion; the firmware callback leaves peer ACK unconfirmed. The installed supplicant rejected Neighbor Report locally because its RRM connection state was unset. No RRM/BTM peer exchange was established. AP-initiated BTM/802.11v and 802.11r, forged-frame protection, throughput and sustained reliability remain unverified.

Type-C USB-OTG ROM connection and complete 16 MiB NOR readback were verified with esptool 5.6.0. The board kernel has no S31 USB OTG role/controller integration. Dedicated package pads 44/45 are USB_D+/USB_D−, separate from GPIO44 LCD reset and GPIO45 audio PA enable. Host VBUS/CC role and power behavior are not verified; this does not establish EmberBSD USB support.

On one V1.2 sample, the standard CO5300 framebuffer/genfb/LVGL path displayed a visible interface after the published two-row RASET fix; the user also confirmed changing touch coordinates. This is one RAM-only scenario, not acceptance of other revisions. A later normal POWER boot with the R3 root displayed the fixed MOSAICO, 21 C and SUNNY LVGL sample on a dark background. A separate EmberBSD QML run completed two presentations (initial 21 C and updated -8) in one process, with one 468 KiB RSS sample; the -8 appearance was not visually confirmed. The LVGL display result does not apply to the QML run. The weather samples do not read sensors or online weather. Touch orientation/calibration, audio playback and sustained operation remain unverified. Factory camera preview is vendor-firmware evidence; EmberBSD has a target-built SC101IOT sensor/DVP/video(4) path, but no physical EmberBSD frame has been captured. The mode table requires 20 MHz XCLK and names 15 fps; fitted oscillator frequency and actual frame rate are unmeasured. EmberBSD radio evidence includes bounded WPA2/SAE handshakes and small/1400-byte gateway ICMP reachability on one sample; one bounded roam succeeded; repeated roaming and sustained operation remain unverified.

The BMI270, two BMM150 sensors and BQ27220 have native envsys drivers included in a target-linked ESP_MOSAICO_SC101IOT_WIFI kernel. Physical readings from these drivers have not been tested; prior BMI270 identification-register reads do not establish motion sampling.
S31 I2S/AHB-DMA and ES8311 drivers are present and the combined ESP_MOSAICO_SC101IOT_WIFI kernel linked. No physical playback or capture has been tested.

The board tree enables SPI3 and the published source adds a read-only NAND ID/status utility with a staged RV32 binary. It has not been run on hardware or installed in a root image; NAND data reads, ECC, bad-block management, filesystems and boot are not established.

On one V1.2 sample, the left-slot camera EEPROM descriptor had valid CRCs and hardware-version field 0x0102. The factory firmware separately reported SC101IOT PID 0xda4a and rendered a changing 1280 × 720 UYVY preview. The optional EmberBSD driver read SC101IOT PID 0xda4a at 0x68 in a RAM trial. Published source now adds a target-built 640 × 480 UYVY sensor/DVP/video(4) path, but no physical EmberBSD frame has been captured. Its mode table requires 20 MHz XCLK and names 15 fps; fitted oscillator frequency and actual frame rate are unmeasured. The factory and EmberBSD results apply only to this sample and do not establish sensor identity for other modules.
